findings.issue: Group 2 excludes internal/query/databases_test.go:56 with the rationale that adding 190000 'would re-run an identical query and assert nothing new'. That rationale is wrong for this site: unlike the three io_test.go string-inspection loops in the same table, :56 IS a live-connection loop (postgres.NewTestConnectVersion at :64) and it is the ONLY place PgStatDatabaseSessionsDefault is ever executed against a server — the general loop at :34 exercises SelectStatDatabaseGeneralQuery only. Excluding it leaves one production query with zero PG 19 live coverage in a feature whose entire premise is 'run every existing query against PG 19'.
findings.fix: Either move databases_test.go:56 into Group 1 (append 190000, keeping 140000 as the lower bound: []int{140000, 190000}), or keep the exclusion but replace the rationale with an honest one and record it as an explicit deferred item in the decisions log. The current wording will make a reviewer believe the site is a string-inspection loop like the io_test ones.

findings.issue: Task 05 has no TDD Anchor section at all (tasks 04 and 06 both have one). The task states 'Nothing in the test suite can catch a mistake here' and makes eye-verification the sole gate — verified: Test_describeReport (report/report_test.go:1170) compares describeReport() output against the very constants it renders, so any text edit passes by construction. However, the specific failure mode the task fears (row in the wrong slot, missing Note) IS cheaply testable without a golden: the constants are package-level strings in the same package as the tests.
findings.fix: Add a TDD Anchor with a small ordering test in package report, e.g. for each of the three constants assert strings.Index(c, "- started_by") lies between Index("- relation") and Index("- state") (Index("- backup_type") between "- duration" and "- state"), that "- mode" follows "- started_by" in the vacuum constant, and that each constant contains a 'PostgreSQL 19' Note line positioned before the 'Details:' block. That is ~20 lines and converts the whole 'invisible to CI' argument into a guarded invariant. If the team still prefers eye-only verification, say so explicitly as a deviation instead of leaving the section absent.

findings.issue: Group 3 instruction says 'each of these selectors' newest branch is >= PostgresV18 (or lower)' and that a 190000 row 'proves this feature did not accidentally move a boundary'. For two of the eight tables that is not what the code does: SelectStatReplicationSlotsQuery (internal/query/replication_slots.go:39) and SelectStatIOTimeQuery (internal/query/io.go:99) take the version as `_ int` and ignore it entirely — there is no branch to derive from and the new row cannot pin any boundary; it is a trivially-green regression pin. An implementer following 'open the selector next to the test and read its branch conditions' will look for a branch that does not exist.
findings.fix: Note in the Group 3 table that replication_slots and io_time selectors are version-independent (signature `_ int`), so their 190000 rows are constant-value pins, not boundary proofs. The six remaining tables (bgwriter >=V18, wal >=V18, io >=V18, statements timing/JIT/report >=170000) do have branches, and all eight proposed expected values were independently verified correct.

findings.issue: Implementation hints prescribe scanned,KiB 1000 -> 1500 (delta 500) plus a sentinel `assert.Contains(out, "500")` copied from the bgwriter model (report_record_bgwriter_test.go:228). "500" is a substring of the cumulative value "1500" that the same cell prints when DiffIntvl is stale — i.e. the sentinel still passes under the exact regression the pg19 subcase exists to catch. The golden comparison does catch it, so the test is sound, but the sentinel adds no localisation value for the failure it was placed to localise.
findings.fix: Pick a delta that is not a substring of any fixture value in the row (e.g. 1000 -> 1700, delta 700, keeping the same delta across both subcases), or assert on a value only reachable through the diff path. Keep the pid Contains sentinel as-is.
